chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Isma'il ibn Marar and Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Mubarak from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had to fast two consecutive months, so he fasted twenty-five days, then he got sick; when he recovered, does he complete (build upon) what he fasted, or does he repeat his fasting entirely? He said, 'Rather, he completes what he had fasted.' Then he said, 'This is what God has overridden, and there is nothing upon what God has overridden.'

key_terms.غَلَبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: What God has overridden (excused by God)

ai.seo_question: Does illness break the continuity of consecutive fasting days for expiation, requiring a restart?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that for expiatory fasts requiring continuity, illness constitutes a valid interruption where the fasted days are preserved rather than lost, distinguishing this from voluntary fasts. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that 'what God has overwhelmed one with' (ghalib) exempts one from strict continuity, emphasizing divine mercy in legal obligations. The hadith underscores the balance between maintaining ritual integrity and accommodating human frailty within the framework of kaffarah.
